issues.title: Arbitrary samples lack a common point-evaluation domain

failure_location.quote: Given arbitrary sample points $\by_1,\ldots,\by_k \in U$ and functions $h_1,\ldots,h_k \in L_2(U,\CC;\mu)$

issues.failure_explanation: The theorem claims the scalar/Hilbert-valued error equality for sampling at arbitrary points of U. The old assumptions only imply that the kernel diagonal is finite almost everywhere; an exceptional point can have undefined or unbounded evaluation, and an L2 equivalence class has no representation-independent value there. Consequently S_n^X and A^X=I^X-S_n^X need not be well-defined bounded operators, so Lemma lemma:norms-linear-operators cannot be applied as claimed.
issues.overall_effect: The sampling-error equality and the sampling-width and least-squares chains built from it are not well-defined until a common representative and admissible evaluation domain are fixed.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Fix measurable representatives of the basis and define the full-measure set U₀ = {y ∈ U : Σ_s σ_s^{-2}|φ_s(y)|² < ∞}. For y ∈ U₀, define each H_{X,σ} function by its convergent coefficient series, restrict the sampling points and sampling-width families throughout the affected chain to U₀, and use the resulting bounded-evaluation estimate to justify the coefficient-matrix representation needed by Lemma lemma:norms-linear-operators.
issues.why_classification: This is not a transcriptional error because a common representative, bounded evaluation, and the applicability of the operator lemma require mathematical verification. The repair is nevertheless a short standard finite-trace and Cauchy–Schwarz argument; it excludes only a null set on which the original sampling operation was not coherent and leaves the least-squares methods, conclusions, rates, and probability guarantees unchanged.

issues.title: The least-squares weight matrix has the wrong dimension
issues.failure_explanation: The data vector and L have cn rows, whereas W=diag(omega_1,...,omega_n) is n-by-n. Thus L^*WL and L^*W(f(y_i)) cannot be multiplied when c>1, independently of whether an inverse or pseudoinverse is used.
issues.overall_effect: The stated S_{cn} least-squares construction and all convergence results invoking it are dimensionally undefined for the oversampling factors used in the paper.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace W = diag(ω₁,…,ω_n) by W = diag(ω₁,…,ω_{cn}) in the least-squares coefficient formula and read every dependent invocation with this corrected c n-by-c n matrix.
issues.why_classification: The old source explicitly supplies c n samples, c n weights, a matrix L with c n rows, and a data vector of length c n. These dimensions uniquely force the missing upper index c n, so the error is purely transcriptional and its correction changes no argument or guarantee.

issues.title: Ordinary inverse fails for admissible rank-deficient least-squares data
issues.failure_explanation: Take c=1 and choose all admitted weights to be zero. Then the objective in least-squares-sampling1 is identically zero, the normal matrix L^*WL is zero, and its displayed inverse does not exist. Repeated or otherwise linearly dependent sample rows give further admissible examples. Thus the old coefficient formula does not define the advertised least-squares output on its stated input domain.
issues.overall_effect: The generic least-squares construction has no output for admissible rank-deficient systems, although its full-rank specialization remains valid.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the coefficient map by (W^{1/2}L)^+W^{1/2} applied to the data vector, equivalently by (L*WL)^+L*W, and interpret arg min as the minimum-coefficient-norm least-squares minimizer.
issues.why_classification: The sentence immediately preceding the defective display already says that the Moore–Penrose inverse is to be used. Thus the ordinary inverse symbol is uniquely contradicted by the old source itself, and replacing it by the stated pseudoinverse is the forced transcriptional correction; it defines the advertised output on rank-deficient inputs without a new assumption, proof, or weakened guarantee.

issues.title: Off-by-one indexing makes the GPC basis undefined

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Here $\FF$ is the set of all sequences of non-negative integers

issues.failure_explanation: The old source defines the Jacobi and Hermite sequences only for orders in N_0 but sets the univariate factor varphi_k equal to the polynomial of order k-1. The GPC construction then evaluates varphi_{s_j} for multiindex components s_j in N_0. In particular, s_j=0 requires varphi_0=J_{-1} or H_{-1}, so the labeled GPC expansion and its asserted tensor basis are not defined.
issues.overall_effect: The tensor GPC basis, its coefficients, the specialized weighted balls, and the formal application results using them lack a defined zero-order factor.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Retain the one-based univariate notation and replace each tensor factor φ_{s_j} by φ_{s_j+1}, so that the factor of degree s_j is J_{s_j} or H_{s_j}; use this same indexing in the GPC coefficients, weighted balls, and all dependent specialized results.
issues.why_classification: The sequences are explicitly indexed by nonnegative polynomial degree and the multiindices have components in N₀, so the zero component uniquely requires the constant polynomial J₀ or H₀. The corrected tensor factor is forced by the old definitions and standard basis assertion, and no inference or substantive guarantee changes.

issues.title: The specialized weight-class premise is empty

failure_location.quote: For a set  $\bsigma=(\sigma_\bs)_{\bs \in \FF}\in\ell_q(\NN)$ of positive numbers such that $\norm{\bsigma^{-1}}{\ell_q(\NN)} \le N$, denote by $B_{X,\bsigma}^q(M,N)$

diagnostic_evidence.quote: For a set  $\bsigma=(\sigma_\bs)_{\bs \in \FF}\in\ell_q(\NN)$ of positive numbers such that $\norm{\bsigma^{-1}}{\ell_q(\NN)} \le N$, denote by $B_{X,\bsigma}^q(M,N)$

issues.failure_explanation: The prose claims that the positive infinite family bsigma itself lies in ell_q and that bsigma^{-1} also lies in ell_q. The old paper's earlier abstract definition actually supports weighted balls under inverse summability alone. Materially, the specialized claim describes no admissible family: at every index sigma_bs^q+sigma_bs^{-q}>=2, so both sums cannot be finite over the infinite set F. Thus the specialized class is empty rather than the nonempty inverse-summable class needed by the applications.
issues.overall_effect: The tensor-product specialization is vacuous, and the weights supplied by the application lemmas do not meet its stated extra premise, so the stated route to the application theorems is broken.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Delete the premise that σ itself belongs to ℓ_q. Define the specialized ball for any positive family indexed by F satisfying ||σ^{-1}||_{ℓ_q(F)} ≤ N, enumerate the countable set F when applying the abstract theorem, and use that definition in the dependent application results.
issues.why_classification: The earlier abstract definition and every application use inverse summability alone, while a positive infinite family and its reciprocal cannot both lie in ℓ_q. The old source therefore uniquely identifies the extra membership phrase as stray text; removing it loses no coherent case and requires no new mathematical argument.

issues.title: Log-normal inverse-weight summability needs a truncation-order threshold

failure_location.quote: Then we have that for any $\eta \in \NN$,

issues.failure_explanation: For a fixed j and multiindices bs=k e_j, the old definition gives sigma_{k e_j}^2=1+k rho_j^2 when eta=1. Therefore sum_k sigma_{k e_j}^{-q} diverges for q<=2. More generally, sigma_{k e_j}^{-q} is asymptotic to k^{-eta q/2}, so inverse-weight summability requires eta q/2>1. Admissible data exist, for example rho_j=2^j and psi_j=0, so this is an internal counterexample rather than a missing external fact.
issues.overall_effect: The inverse-weight premise needed for the log-normal branch of the sampling theorem is not established for the low truncation orders allowed by the old lemma.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Amend the log-normal lemma to require η ∈ N with η > 2/q, justify the inverse-weight summability under this condition by the standard one-dimensional tail and product estimate, and choose such an η when invoking the lemma in theorem:sampling-lognormal-affine.
issues.why_classification: The low-order assertion is coherently false, so this is not a typo. However, η is a freely chosen auxiliary truncation order, and imposing ηq/2 > 1 is a short routine technical qualification that preserves the PDE class, weighted-summability conclusion needed downstream, sampling method, convergence rate, and probability mode.

issues.title: Affine Jacobi weight specification does not support the summability application

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Let  $(J_k)_{k\in \NN_0}$ be the sequence of Jacobi polynomials

issues.failure_explanation: The old statement leaves the factors c_k^(a,b), including the essential zero-degree factor, undefined in its infinite-product weights. Supplying the positive normalization constants printed in v6 alone does not establish the full summability contract: the cited weighted coefficient estimate uses their reciprocals, and merely positive radii do not ensure inverse-weight summability. For example, take a=b=0, q=1, bar a=1, all psi_j=0, rho_1=1/2, and rho_j=j^2 for j>=2. The displayed radius hypotheses hold and the PDE is uniformly elliptic, but inserting c_k=sqrt(2k+1) gives sigma_(k e_1)^(-1)=2^k/sqrt(2k+1), which is not summable. These are checks on completeness of the proposed normalization repair, not a claim that the intended sampling rate is impossible.
issues.overall_effect: The affine weighted ball and its dependent sampling construction are not justified by the weight specification and hypotheses as written. A corrected weight family and admissible-radius choice recover a comparable construction with the same central convergence exponents in the uniformly elliptic regime.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Set c_0^(a,b)=1 and, for k>=1, c_k^(a,b)=[(2k+a+b+1)k! Gamma(k+a+b+1) Gamma(a+1) Gamma(b+1)/(Gamma(k+a+1) Gamma(k+b+1) Gamma(a+b+2))]^(1/2). Use tilde_sigma_nu=product_j rho_j^(nu_j)/c_(nu_j)^(a,b), require rho_j>1, weighted ellipticity ||sum_j rho_j |psi_j|/bar a||_infinity<1, and (rho_j^(-1)) in ell_q. Apply the cited Jacobi weighted estimate (Bachmayr-Cohen-Migliorati, Theorem 3.1 and Remark 3.3, equation (75), arXiv:1509.07045v2) and the inverse-weight product estimate. Reorder the polynomial basis and instantiate the approximation spaces and sampling construction with these corrected weights. The weighted ball and constants change, but the rates (n/log n)^(-1/q), n^(-1/q)sqrt(log n), and n^(-1/q) survive with the same q. For compatibility, make uniform ellipticity theta_0=||sum_j |psi_j|/bar a||_infinity<1 explicit. Given an old admissible radius sequence with weighted bound theta_rho<1, choose r_j=1+epsilon rho_j with theta_0+epsilon theta_rho<1; then r_j>1 and sum_j r_j^(-q)<=epsilon^(-q)sum_j rho_j^(-q). This preserves the standard uniformly elliptic model class after reselecting auxiliary radii, not every literal old radius. The author revision supplies the constants but still multiplies by them and allows merely positive radii, so it is incomplete repair evidence.
issues.why_classification: Defining the missing constants alone fails to resolve the complete recorded chain. The cited Jacobi estimate supplies sum_nu (tilde_sigma_nu ||u_nu||_V)^2<infinity. For fixed Jacobi parameters the constants grow at most polynomially, and the product formula sum_nu tilde_sigma_nu^(-q)=product_j(1+sum_(k>=1)c_k^q rho_j^(-qk)) is finite: rho_j>1 with inverse radii in ell_q gives inf_j rho_j>1 and inner tails bounded by C rho_j^(-q). Correcting the weights and admissibility and rebuilding the dependent sampling construction is contained specialist work preserving the central rates in the uniformly elliptic regime. This supports moderate, without claiming global new architecture or unchanged literal weight assumptions.
